primary_result: The outcome-blind complete Haze4K official-test census passed every frozen structural and isolation gate. All 1,000 haze and 1,000 clear files paired, decoded, and aligned; decoded-RGB identity yielded exactly 250 canonical clear scenes with four haze variants each. Fixed-salt ranking assigned 100 scenes and 400 observations to development screening and 150 scenes and 600 observations to candidate confirmation, with disjoint exact hard-linked role assets and assignment digest 6ca5174470dad2b4eef4ae15c5a13a99d8ae9fc0bc2ea1116b199c4d4bc05582.
gate_reasons: all 1,000 haze and 1,000 clear files were loader-paired, decoded, and dimension aligned without failure
the complete census recovered exactly 250 canonical decoded-RGB clear scenes and exactly four haze observations per scene
the frozen salt produced disjoint 100-scene development and 150-scene candidate-confirmation roles covering all 1,000 observations
both route-owned role assets passed exact count, same-file identity, exact-name pairing, and cross-role containment checks
no model, checkpoint, inference, restoration metric, local-error metric, threshold analysis, or candidate comparison was accessed
competing_explanation: Decoded RGB equality is a valid deterministic leakage-control identity but does not establish original capture provenance or the physical meaning of filename suffixes. The four clear aliases may reflect dataset packaging. The full test is also baseline-exposed through prior reproduction of the official aggregate ConvIR-B metric, so the preserved status is candidate-unseen rather than wholly outcome-unseen.
limitations: This qualification is structure-only and contains no evidence about local restoration errors or image quality.
Only the 100-scene development asset is authorized for the next fixed-baseline replication; the 150-scene candidate-confirmation asset remains prohibited for development.
Per-image assignments and role assets remain cloud-only; GitHub retains only aggregate evidence and the assignment digest.
Canonical scene grouping prevents duplicated-clear leakage but does not assert independent acquisition provenance.
